newsitem.title: USA: Apple junk bonds down on expected loss.
newsitem.headline: Apple junk bonds down on expected loss.

text.p: Prices of the junk bonds of Apple Computer Inc dropped as much as five points on Monday on news the company expects to take a $100 to $150 million loss due to poor demand for its computer products.
"Considering their already low dollar price, that's a pretty significant move for these bonds," said one trader.

Prices on Apple's 6 1/2 percent senior notes due 2004 dropped as low as 82-84 from 87-88 in morning trading, said one junk trader. Another trader said the bonds had risen to 84 1/2-88 around noon time.
Apple has $300 million of the senior notes outstanding.
Apple also has over $600 million of convertible bonds outstanding. Prices on the convertible bonds had dropped to 89 3/4 from 99 3/4 as of midday, a trader said.
Traders note hedge fund investors had begun to buy the convertibles, despite the slide in their prices.
"There is an arbitrage play going on here. People are buying Apple's convertible (bonds) and shorting the stock and the senior notes," said one trader.

A trader speculated that hedge fund investors were favoring the convertible bonds because they offer a better total return than the company's junk bonds, as well as more credit protection than Apple's common stock.
Apple's stock price was down four percent to 17 3/4 as of 1300EST/1800GMT.
Apple's senior notes are rated B1/B+ and its convertible debt is rated B3/B-.
Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's have had a negative outlook on the credit rating for Apple debt for many months.
Craig Fitt, an analyst who follows Apple for Moody's, declined to comment on whether or not recent news about the company's earnings would affect its ratings.
Molly Toll-Reed, the Standard & Poor's analyst who follows Apple, declined any comment.
